name: Shaft
author: E. T. Carter
description: Volumetric light rays: a dense fan of soft, near-parallel shafts pours from a source just off the top corner and rakes down across the whole frame, broad bright sheets carrying many fine striations with feathered edges. Dust motes drift down the beams through a slow turbulent haze, two fainter fans sit behind the first for depth, and a dim tinted fog fills the gaps so no corner goes dead.

params.label: Drift speed
params.effect: Pace at which rays slide across the fan and the haze and dust roll down the beams; 0 holds a still frame.

params.label: Ray density
params.effect: How many shafts cross the fan; low gives a few broad sheets of light, high packs in many fine slivers.

params.label: Dust
params.effect: Amount of visible dust in the beam, both the drifting motes and the turbulent thickening of the haze; 0 leaves clean smooth rays.

params.label: Fog
params.effect: Ambient tinted fog between and beyond the rays; low drops the gaps toward black, high fills the frame with luminous atmosphere.

params.label: Source X
params.effect: Horizontal position of the light source as a fraction of frame width; negative sits it off the left edge, past 1 off the right.

params.label: Source Y
params.effect: Vertical position of the light source (1 is the top edge); above 1 it sits off the top so the rays rake down into the frame.

params.label: Light intensity
params.effect: Overall brightness of rays, dust and fog; low gives faint moody shafts, high floods the frame with light.
